test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Robert, Chris and Jeremy can finish a certain piece of work in 10, 14 and 21 days,respectively. All three of them started the work together. Robert left the work after 5 days and Chris left just 2 days before the work was completed. Find the total number of days taken for the work to be completed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Work** be LCM of (10, 14, 21) = 210 units.

Efficiencies: **Robert** = 21, **Chris** = 15, **Jeremy** = 10.

Robert worked for 5 days: 21 × 5 = 105 units. Remaining = 210 − 105 = 105 units.

If Chris stayed till the end, he would do extra work for 2 days: 15 × 2 = 30 units.

Total units for Chris and Jeremy combined = 105 + 30 = 135 units.

Total days = 135 ÷ (15 + 10) = 135 ÷ 25 = 5.4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Robert (R) = 10 days, Chris (C) = 14 days, Jeremy (J) = 21 days.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency × Time = Total Work.

⇒ Work done by **Robert** in 5 days = 21 × 5 = 105 units.

⇒ Let total days be **x**. Jeremy worked for **x** days and Chris worked for **(x − 2)** days.

⇒ 105 + 15 × (x − 2) + 10 × x = 210

⇒ 105 + 15x − 30 + 10x = 210

⇒ 25x + 75 = 210

⇒ 25x = 135

⇒ x = 135 ÷ 25 = 5.4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leaving Work Before Completion

If a person leaves **n days before** completion, add their n days of work to the total work and divide by the combined efficiency of the remaining group.

LCM Method for Total Work

Always assume **Total Work** as the LCM of time taken by individuals to avoid complex fraction calculations.

Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. Efficiency = Work ÷ Time.</p
